newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles panel close to issuing arena report.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles panel close to issuing arena report.

text.p: A Los Angeles city panel planned to hold a hearing Monday on a proposed sports and entertainment complex before issuing its long-awaited recommendations to the city council, a city official said.
Los Angeles city officials have been negotiating for months for the development of a downtown arena for the Los Angeles Kings hockey team and the Lakers basketball team.

Following Monday's public hearing, the city's ad hoc committee on the arena proposal was expected to send its recommendations to the city council for review, said Pat Healy, the committee's chief legislative assistant.
The Los Angeles City Council could act on the recommendations as early as January 15, Healy said.

Under the latest proposal, the city would contribute $70.5 million to the project. Its contribution would be funded with a taxable debt financing for $50.5 million and $20 million from a bond reserve fund.
The annual debt service costs and lost interest earnings to the bond reserve fund would total about $6.8 million, according to a three-page summary of the proposal.
